source_text: . Unde autem id ostenderem, paulo post adhibui, quod mihi visum est grande documentum. negantes Dei dona esse virtutes quibus recte vivitur, et eas naturae voluntatique humanae, non gratiae Dei tribuentes, hoc uti argumento, quod eas nonnumquam habeant infideles
pass_a_gloss: . whence however it ostenderem, paulo after adhibui, that/which to-me visum is grande documentum. they-deny of-God gifts to-be virtutes to-whom rightly lives, and them of-nature voluntatique humanae, not of-grace of-God tribuentes, this uti argumento, that/which them nonnumquam habeant infideles.

lemmas.lexica: LS/Blaise natura=created constitution, not 'original sin' itself
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will
LS gratia=favor; Blaise grace; in iustitia definitions often 'favoritism'

pass_b_english: I pursue the points [in his argument] that seem clever to him.
Eagerly blaming the substance, [he] praises its gifts.

choices.why: Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.
Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
In the suum cuique definition gratia is partiality, not saving grace.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
